scenarios.name: Vague stuckness should name one task
scenarios.message: I have so much to do and I don't know where to begin.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Normalize the stuckness and ask one simple question that helps the user name the one task most on their mind. Do not list suggestions yet.

scenarios.name: Specific stuck task moves toward diagnosis
scenarios.message: I need to start the quarterly report but I keep opening my phone instead.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Capture the quarterly report as targetTask, normalize without shame, and move toward diagnosing why it is stuck with at most one targeted question.
anti_patterns: jumping straight to a generic productivity tip

scenarios.name: Too-big blocker gets one physical first action

history.content: What about cleaning the apartment is making it hard to start?

scenarios.message: It's huge. I don't even know what counts as starting.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Identify blockerType too_big and offer one tiny visible physical first action, such as putting one dish in the sink or opening one trash bag. Do not offer alternatives.
anti_patterns: asking the user to break it down themselves
continuing diagnosis after the blocker is clear

scenarios.name: Too-boring blocker gets a dopamine constraint
scenarios.message: The receipts are easy. They're just so boring that I can't make myself care.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Identify blockerType too_boring and offer one concrete constraint such as a five-minute timer, location shift, or body-double style cue.
anti_patterns: telling the user to care about consequences

scenarios.name: Decision paralysis removes the choice
scenarios.message: I have emails, laundry, a proposal, and tax stuff, and I keep switching without doing any of them.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Identify blockerType decision_paralysis, pick one task plainly, and say the others can wait. Do not ask the user to choose between all of them.
anti_patterns: asking the user to rank all tasks
choosing more than one first task

scenarios.name: Shame spiral hands off to emotional regulation
scenarios.message: I hate myself. I always ruin things. I can't think and I feel like a complete failure.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Detect emotional_flooding and hand off to Emotional Regulation without pushing productivity or a first action.
anti_patterns: telling the user to calm down so they can work

scenarios.name: Unrelated project review request hands off
scenarios.message: Actually can you review my whole project list and tell me what matters this week?
scenarios.expected_behavior: Recognize this is outside Task Initiation and return handoff rather than forcing a tiny first action.
anti_patterns: choosing one task from the project list without enough context

scenarios.name: Accepted first action moves to commit

state.firstAction: open the document and write one rough sentence

history.content: The move is: open the document and write one rough sentence.

scenarios.expected_behavior: Move to commit by asking one question about what they will do and when. Keep the action concrete and do not add new advice.
anti_patterns: completing before the timeframe is stated

scenarios.name: User's own first action is accepted

history.content: The first move is to open the email and read only the first line.

scenarios.message: Maybe I'll just draft the first sentence instead.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Accept the user's proposed firstAction and ask one commit question about when they will do it.
anti_patterns: arguing for the coach's original action
treating the user's idea as wrong

scenarios.name: Task creation is not done unless clearly requested
scenarios.message: I can't start packing for the trip. Maybe remind me later too.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Focus on task initiation unless the user clearly asks to create or update an app object; do not invent a reminder or task action. Ask at most one relevant question.
anti_patterns: turning the flow into task management

scenarios.name: Action plus timeframe completes the skill

state.firstAction: set a 5-minute timer and open the invoice tab

history.content: What are you doing, and when?

scenarios.message: I'll set the timer and open the invoice tab now.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Confirm the commitment in one sentence and complete the skill with firstAction and timeframe in state.

scenarios.name: Explicit cancellation ends the skill
scenarios.message: I don't want to do this right now. Stop.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Respect the stop request and cancel the skill without coaching or asking another question.
anti_patterns: asking why they want to stop
